labels.notes: Main theorem Causal.Causality.not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeA_of_isClosed_le (FlrwTypeClosedAmbient.lean:289) is the target's title exactly: [T2Space M], IsClosed {z : M × M | C.le ⊤ z.1 z.2} (the conclusion shape of GloballyHyperbolic.isClosed_le, GlobalHyperbolicity.lean:116), C.IsCausal (Properties.lean:95, antisymmetry of ≤_M), hA, conclusion ∀ Ũ p, ¬ C.PastBoundaryChart W Ũ p. No (B), future one-connectedness, causal arc-connectedness or second countability. hA is textually FlrwType.lean:318–319, hB textually :320; confirmed in an audit probe that passed the same hA, hB variables to not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType and to both new theorems. The local forms' closedness hypothesis is textually IsCausallyClosedOn U (scaffold/CausalScaffold/GerochEquiv.lean:108–110), inlined. The corollary (:303) goes through hG.isClosed_le hT and hG.1, which is IsCausal (GloballyHyperbolic := IsCausal ∧ compact diamonds, Properties.lean:144). The time-reversed (A) and (B) binders match not_futureBoundaryChart_of_flrwType (FlrwType.lean:362–364). The (B) forms add [SecondCountableTopology M] and CausallyArcConnectedOn W. They are needed by the library's (2.4) (PastInextensible.exists_mem_of_mem_Jplus, PastInextensibleMeetsCauchy.lean:147) and by the split. This is disclosed in the checklist (:68–69), in b_report and in questions; whether they are mathematically necessary is stated as undecided. No label, no ** mark (grep: 0).

checks.layer_1: The one import is Causal.FlrwType. I simulated it in memory per kb/0247: lean_index()['imports'] plus Causal.FlrwTypeClosedAmbient → [Causal.FlrwType]. model_path of the new module and of its one direct import is None. The closure has 49 Causal modules, none in MODEL_LAYER, and holds Causal.GlobalHyperbolicity and Causal.CurvesExtendSecondCountable. import_chain to Causal.Ladder.Rules is None. No statement mentions a metric: timelikeLine and posHalfLine are ETT-layer (Causal.Lines, FlrwType.lean). The hypotheses are standing classes (T2, second countable), the nodes is_causal, globally_hyperbolic and tarentin, the declared (A) and (B), CausallyArcConnectedOn W (from FlrwType's theorem) and '≤ closed', which is a hypothesis and not a node.
checks.false_of_squeeze: Sound. (2): p ≪_Ũ γ̃ s₀ puts p in the open I⁻(γ̃ s₀, Ũ). σ is continuous within Ioc 0 1 at 0, and 𝓝[Ioc 0 1] 0 is NeBot. If σ 0 = p, some σ t with t ∈ (0, 1] is in that set and in I⁺(p, Ũ), against hσK. (3) extends to t = 0 through the relatively closed ≤_U, since p and σ t are in U. (4): the set {(t, s) ∈ [0, 1]² | σ t ≤_U γ̃ s} is closed, so compact. Its projection to s is compact, so closed in ℝ, and contains (0, 1], so it contains 0. That gives σ t̄ ≤_U γ̃ 0 = p. Antisymmetry gives σ t̄ = p, which contradicts (2) if t̄ = 0 and p ∉ W if t̄ > 0. It uses only d.mem, d.not_mem, curve, chronalCurveOn, curve_zero, s₀ and s₀_mem.
checks.A_argument: Sound. Step (a) gives γ̃ and σ past-inextensible and chronal on segments in W over Ioc 0 1. (A) applied twice gives (3) by σ t ∈ ⋃ I⁺(γ̃ s, W) with p ≪_Ũ γ̃ s, and (4) by γ̃ s ∈ ⋃ I⁺(σ t, W). The relations move to U by lt_mono.
checks.B_argument: Sound. For (3), (B) at σ t gives S ⊆ I⁻(σ t, W), and the split puts γ̃ 1 in J⁺(S, W) or J⁻(S, W). In the first case γ̃ meets S at some u ∈ (0, 1] by (2.4), with ≤_W antisymmetric from ≤_U by le_mono, so p ≪ γ̃ u ≪ σ t. In the second, p ≪ γ̃ 1 ≤_W z ≪_W σ t. (4) is symmetric, with σ 1 split and t = 1 in the J⁻ case. Only ≤ is concluded, so no push-up is needed.
checks.fields_used: TRUE as claimed. The module never references futureClosed (grep). Both uses of d.avoid (:258, :411) discard the last conjunct with '-', so it cannot be used later. No library lemma taking d is called, and the fields used are listed in check false_of_squeeze. Field (ii) is used only through d.inside_le.trans inf_le_left (V ≤ W). The REPORT and the docstring record this as evidence bearing on OQ-159 ('presupposes no answer', 'evidence for the OQ, not an answer'). The docstring does not mention OQ-159 and decides nothing. OQ-159 stays OPEN in registers/DECISIONS.md:387.
checks.duplicate_kb0082: Statement for statement a twin. Causal.ErsUniqueness.lean:175 defines SplitBy W S as ∀ q ∈ W, q ∈ C.Jplus W S ∪ C.Jminus W S. With the same [T1Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M], splitBy_of_t1_secondCountable hS q hq and hS.mem_Jplus_union_Jminus hq have the same type; checked both ways in the probe. The names differ, so there is no kb/0082 environment merge, and the twin is disclosed in its docstring (:134–135). Importing Causal.ErsSecondCountable is ETT-layer (model_path None) and creates no cycle: its closure of 57 modules does not contain FlrwType. But it pulls Causal.Ladder.Rules into the leaf's closure through ErsSecondCountable → ErsMughd → Causal.Ladder.Rules, and adds 15 modules. The planner's sequencing evidence relies on the leaf not reaching Rules, so the import is not the right fix for this leaf. Under docs/CAMPAIGN.md ('prove the lemma in your own file and report it') the restatement is the compliant choice now. The clean fix is a hoist, see the findings.

findings.what: IsCauchySurfaceOn.mem_Jplus_union_Jminus is a statement-for-statement twin of splitBy_of_t1_secondCountable (Causal/ErsSecondCountable.lean:158, SplitBy unfolded). It is disclosed and has a different name, so there is no kb/0082 merge. The REPORT suggests importing Causal.ErsSecondCountable 'which is ETT-layer (model_path None)'. It omits that this import makes the leaf downstream of Causal.Ladder.Rules (ErsSecondCountable → ErsMughd → Causal.Ladder.Rules, plus 15 modules), contrary to the planner's evidence that the leaf does not reach Rules.
findings.fix: Keep the restatement in this target. Correct the REPORT note. Plan a hoist: state the W-split once in Causal.CurvesExtendSecondCountable, beside exists_inextensible_of_t1_secondCountable. That module is in both closures and Rules-free, and IsCauchySurfaceOn (Causal.Cauchy) is in its closure. Then re-prove splitBy_of_t1_secondCountable as `fun q hq => hS.mem_Jplus_union_Jminus hq` and delete the twin here.

findings.what: 'In a closed antisymmetric ambient these fields are idle' overstates what is proved, and the sentence is evidence that will reach the author on OQ-159. What is proved is that neither new theorem uses field (iii) or (vi)'s last conjunct. In a closed, causal ambient field (iii) is still load-bearing elsewhere: timelikeLine_not_pastBoundaryChart (FlrwType.lean:544) uses d.futureClosed to exclude every chart with no (A) or (B), and the timelike line is globally hyperbolic and tarentin.
findings.fix: Replace with 'neither theorem uses field (iii) or the last conjunct of (vi); (A), resp. (B), with closedness and antisymmetry make them unnecessary for excluding a chart', and keep 'evidence for OQ-159, not an answer'.

findings.what: The hedge on the (A)-needed direction is redundant and makes the result look weaker than proved. The hedge is 'may alternatively violate second countability or causal arc-connectedness of W', and in the docstring 'On a second countable space with W causally arc-connected'. A witness that (A) is needed for not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType must satisfy that theorem's other hypotheses, which include [SecondCountableTopology M] and CausallyArcConnectedOn W. So not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwTypeB_of_closedIn already excludes every such witness that has ≤_U closed in U × U and antisymmetric for some open U ⊇ W ∪ Ũ. The hedge is not false, only loose, but this finding goes to the author.
findings.fix: State it as: a witness that either of (A), (B) is needed for not_pastBoundaryChart_of_flrwType must have, for every open U ⊇ W ∪ Ũ, ≤_U not closed in U × U or not antisymmetric. Keep the SC and cac caveat only for a hypothetical (B)-only theorem without them.
